Interface: Explicit independent two-state CTMC coordinates with rational parameters, a finite explicit list of target configurations and an explicit product initial law. Additive CDF queries; finite-bin transcript and finite-support sampling guarantees have separate error metrics.
Failure: The continuous first-hit CDF result is an additive approximation, not an exact continuous-time sampler or total-variation guarantee for continuous hit times. Finite-support sampling has an absolute Kolmogorov guarantee. Marked-event transcript results require supplied bins and policy restrictions. The finite interval receipt is one diagnostic; no priority or independent proof certification.

For n independent two-state CTMCs with rational parameters, a list B of m distinct explicit configurations and a product initial law, the source reports a deterministic finite-bit algorithm approximating Pr(H_B<=t) to additive epsilon in time polynomial in input length, m and log(1/epsilon), without enumerating 2^n states. A separate finite-support distribution approximates the full CDF uniformly in absolute Kolmogorov distance, with support size and bit cost polynomial in 1/epsilon; it can be sampled with expected polynomial cost. At fixed rational t>0, a relative approximation for lower-tail CDF values is also claimed. These guarantees do not imply relative accuracy for arbitrarily small upper survival tails, total variation for continuous hit times or exact continuous-time sampling.

The marked-event construction additionally approximates hit-label sub-CDFs and distributions over explicitly supplied time bins. For K-event feedback observing only past labels and those bins, it reports a transcript total-variation guarantee with charged approximation error. It excludes finer continuous-time observations, hidden trajectories and arbitrary nonproduct posteriors.

The packet reports a positive-quadrature boundary-resolvent implementation and one 32-component, two-target Laplace-transform enclosure with width 2^-48; this is not a full exact continuous-time sampler or a full CDF implementation.

Related Astra record N592 covers a single joint target from stationary product initialization. This packet states multi-target additive CDF and marked-bin interfaces from arbitrary product starts. Their proof relationship and comparative novelty require review; this record does not supersede or validate N592.

TARGET-SET RESOLVENT: INTERNAL CANDIDATE THEOREM AND PROOF
2026-10-10.  Status: internally derived proof, not independent certification or priority claim.

Statement and interface
-----------------------
Let X be the product of n independent two-state continuous-time chains. Coordinate i has stationary probability p_i in (0,1) of state 1 and relaxation rate lambda_i>0, all binary-encoded rationals. Thus 0->1 has rate lambda_i p_i and 1->0 has rate lambda_i(1-p_i). Let B be a nonempty list of m distinct explicit n-bit configurations, and let the initial law mu be a product Bernoulli law with binary-rational parameters r_i in [0,1] (deterministic initial configurations are included). Write H_B=inf{t>=0:X_t in B}. Given a nonnegative binary rational t and epsilon in (0,1/2), a deterministic Turing algorithm returns a rational number Fhat(t) satisfying

    |Fhat(t)-Pr_mu(H_B<=t)| <= epsilon

in time polynomial in the total input bit length, m, and log(1/epsilon). It never enumerates the 2^n states. The same construction works whenever the initial law permits poly-time evaluation, to requested precision, of mu^T P_u(:,b) for b in B and has a polynomial-bit upper bound on ||D_pi^{-1/2}mu||. In particular, any explicitly given mixture of polynomially many product laws works.

A separate deterministic preprocessing algorithm produces a finite-support distribution whose CDF is within epsilon uniformly on [0,infinity), with number of support points and bit cost polynomial in the input length, m, and 1/epsilon. It can then draw from that rational distribution using fair bits with polynomial expected cost. This is an absolute Kolmogorov guarantee. It is not exact sampling, a total-variation guarantee, or a relative guarantee for arbitrarily tiny upper survival tails. For any fixed binary-rational t>0, the lower-tail CDF value also admits a relative eta approximation in time polynomial in the input length and log(1/eta), using the explicit positive bound near the end of this note.

MARKED FIRST-HIT EVENTS AND FINITE-BIN FEEDBACK SIMULATION
2026-10-10. Internal construction; no priority or independent-validation claim.
Companion to RESULT.txt. The same supplied product-chain interface and all its bit-cost conventions apply here.

Claim
-----
Let n independent two-state CTMC coordinates have binary-rational p_i in (0,1) and relaxation rates lambda_i>0. Let B={b_1,...,b_m} be distinct explicit configurations, and let the initial law mu be product Bernoulli with binary-rational parameters. For j in [m] define

  F_j(t)=Pr_mu(H_B<=t, X_{H_B}=b_j),
  p_j=Pr_mu(X_{H_B}=b_j)=F_j(infinity).

Given a binary-rational t>=0 and alpha in (0,1/2), each F_j(t) and p_j can be returned as rationals with absolute error at most alpha in deterministic time polynomial in input bits, m, and log(1/alpha). No 2^n-state object is formed. Consequently, for any explicit finite list of binary-rational time-bin endpoints, a rational joint law of (first-hit label, time bin) can be produced within total variation eta in time polynomial in the input, m, bin count, and log(1/eta). The distribution can be sampled exactly from fair bits at expected polynomial cost.

For a K-event feedback experiment, suppose the policy sees only previous first-hit labels and time bins. At each event it chooses new binary-rational coordinate parameters and either starts from the just-hit configuration or supplies a new binary-rational product reset law. Assume this policy is computable in polynomial time and that all generated parameter bit lengths, target-list lengths, bin counts, and transcript encodings remain polynomially bounded in the stated input and K. Approximating each conditional marked-event kernel within eta/K total variation gives a simulator whose complete length-K observed transcript law is within eta total variation of the true policy experiment. Runtime is polynomial in K, n, m, the policy/input bit lengths, maximum bin count, and log(K/eta). The physical waiting times may be exponentially large; runtime has no factor proportional to them or to 1/pi(B).

This theorem concerns the discrete observations of labels and supplied bins. It does not supply exact continuous hit times or a total-variation approximation to their continuous law. CERTIFIED SMALL-BOUNDARY RESOLVENT PRIMITIVE
2026-10-10

Scope
-----
solver.py implements a positive log-time quadrature for the free resolvent
of an independent product of two-state continuous-time chains.  It returns
exact rational interval endpoints for the symmetrized boundary resolvent
K_B(s), the initial-law cross row w_mu(s), and the boundary hitting Laplace
transform.  The dense linear algebra is only m by m; no product state is
enumerated.  Inputs to certified_boundary_resolvent are exact Fractions.

The recorded instance has n=12, m=2, p_i=1/2, heterogeneous relaxation rates
3/4, 1, 5/4, ..., 7/2, product initial probabilities r_i=(i+1)/(i+3),
B={0,4095}, and s=2^-12.  Thus the implicit state space has 4096 states.
The run used 9,915 positive log-time nodes and completed in 6.44 seconds on
the recorded host.  The receipt contains the exact entries and all input
rationals.

Formula evaluated
------------------
For D=diag(pi), A=-D^(1/2) Q D^(-1/2), and beta_z=sqrt(pi(z)), define

    K_B(s) = [ (sI+A)^(-1) ]_{B,B},
    w_mu(s) = mu^T (sI-Q)^(-1)[:,B],
    c_z(s) = w_mu(s)_z / beta_z.

The strong Markov property gives

    E_mu exp(-s H_B) = c(s) K_B(s)^(-1) beta.

At each positive node u, K's integrand is e^(-su)[e^(-uA)]_{B,B}.  Its
entries are products of the two-state heat-kernel factors.  The cross-row
integrand is e^(-su) mu^T P_u(:,B), also evaluated as a product of scalar
two-state probabilities.  Every quadrature weight is positive.

trapezoid for alpha>0 is

Poisson summation and the Mellin transform give

    alpha Q_h(alpha) = sum_{ell in Z} Gamma(1-2 pi i ell/h)
                                      alpha^(2 pi i ell/h).

For y real, |Gamma(1+iy)|^2=pi y/sinh(pi y).  Since
h<1/J and pi>3, t=2 pi^2 ell/h>18 J ell for ell>=1.  Using

Fourier terms by
